P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Residents are subject to exchange controls. The Bahamian dollar is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar, and individuals and corporations residing in The Bahamas are subject to capital or exchange controls (trade.gov). How foreign service fees are received and whether they must be converted under Central Bank rules was not captured.

sources.title: Bahamas (The) Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: individuals and corporations residing in The Bahamas are subject to capital or exchange controls.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Restricted (exchange controls). Resident foreign-currency accounts, whether held in The Bahamas or abroad, may only receive foreign-currency revenue or approved loan proceeds, and may only pay obligations outside The Bahamas that are in foreign currency; other uses are not permitted unless exceptionally approved by the Central Bank. Accounts held abroad by residents need the Central Bank's specific prior approval (Central Bank of The Bahamas notice, 31 March 2026). TRAP for freelancers: you cannot simply keep USD earnings in a local USD account for general use. Get approval through your bank and keep records of the foreign-currency revenue.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: The Bahamas does not tax income (TaxAtlas). Deloitte 2026 agrees: there is no individual income tax, so individuals have no income-tax filing obligations.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 10% (cut from 12% on 1 January 2022). A business registers once taxable supplies exceed BSD 100,000 in any 12-month period. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Bahamian consumers must register regardless of turnover and charge 10% on B2C sales; B2B supplies use the reverse charge.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (6) Local official channel: Resident foreign-currency accounts are allowed only for foreign-currency revenue and foreign obligations. Ask your bank to open and approve one for your export earnings (Central Bank of The Bahamas), and keep the invoices that show the money is your revenue (P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
